content.text: In regions like Nigeria and Venezuela, conventional payment platforms like Stripe and PayPal are often unavailable, leaving digital [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creator-built-how-creators-ghana-get-paid|COREMERCH guide to creator]]s without effective means to monetize their work. This guide outlines how to build a robust [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-10|crypto]] store using [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-explained-digital-15|Cloudflare R2]] Pages without reliance on these platforms. You will learn how to deploy your online store with automatic crypto payment processing and data ownership, empowering you to sell digital products directly to your audience.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The traditional payment ecosystem is riddled with barriers for digital creators, particularly in countries facing financial isolation. COREMERCH's infrastructure is designed to bypass these issues by leveraging freely available tools. Using Cloudflare Pages, you establish your store's hosting layer, while NOWPayments handles crypto transactions seamlessly. This setup empowers you, offering true ownership over your digital commerce without the risk of platform dependency or sudden access loss.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you start deployment, ensure you have the necessary accounts and tools. Create a Cloudflare account to access Cloudflare Pages and Workers. Set up a GitHub account for version control and hosting your website. You'll also need a NOWPayments account for processing cryptocurrency transactions. Your product files should be ready for delivery, and if you're utilizing Supabase for storage, create an account there to manage your orders effectively.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Begin by configuring your Cloudflare Pages environment. Deploy your frontend using GitHub for version control and updates. Next, set up Cloudflare Workers to handle the backend logic, including integrating NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification. Use Supabase to store your order data. Ensure you have set up webhooks correctly so that product delivery is automated once payments are confirmed. This pipeline is critical for a smooth customer experience.
Complete ownership means no platform lock-in.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your payment and delivery systems are in place, it's time to go live. Push your code to GitHub, triggering a deployment to Cloudflare Pages. Test your payment process with a small transaction using NOWPayments to ensure everything works as expected. Monitor the order data in Supabase to confirm that orders are processed correctly. Once you verify the functionality, promote your store online to reach your audience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
Automate payment processing with minimal fees.

Both result in the same ownership structure: your GitHub or Cloudflare account, your Supabase database, your NOWPayments account, your wallet, your store. See both options at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Follow the setup sequence without skipping steps — configuration errors are significantly harder to diagnose than setup time. First: create your NOWPayments account, add wallet addresses, generate your API key, and note your IPN secret key. Second: deploy the backend — configure Cloudflare Worker with your NOWPayments credentials and product settings, or configure Google Apps Script with the same — and confirm the endpoint URL. Third: set the webhook endpoint URL in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Fourth: deploy the storefront to Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages and confirm product pages and checkout display correctly. Fifth: configure your custom domain and DNS if using one. Sixth: complete a real mainnet test transaction. Seventh: check the order database for the test entry. Only after steps six and seven pass cleanly should you share the store URL publicly.

Start by creating a Cloudflare account for hosting and using GitHub for version control. Set up NOWPayments for processing crypto transactions and automate delivery using Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. This ensures you have a fully functional store without the need for traditional payment platforms.
What is the difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 in COREMERCH?

Stack 01 utilizes GitHub Pages and Apps Script for a quick deployment in 4-6 hours, whereas Stack 02 employs Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Supabase for a more robust architecture, deployed in 48 hours, offering greater scalability and features.
Can I host a digital product store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages?

Yes, both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages are excellent options for hosting your digital product store. They provide reliable hosting solutions that integrate seamlessly with other services like NOWPayments for payment processing.
What tools do I need to set up my store?

You need a Cloudflare account for hosting, a GitHub account for version control, and a NOWPayments account for processing payments. Additionally, having Supabase for order management will enhance your store's efficiency.
How long does it take to deploy my store?
Deploying your store using Stack 01 can take between 4-6 hours, while Stack 02 is set up by COREMERCH in just 48 hours, ensuring it is end-to-end tested before you take ownership.
